newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Life members vote to go public.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Life members vote to go public.

text.p: Members of Swiss mutual insurance company Swiss Life/Rentenanstalt voted overwhelmingly in favour of management's proposal to make the group a public limited company, finalising the transformation, Swiss Life said.
"The transition of the mutual insurance company into a public limited company became legally effective with registration in the commercial register on June 30,1997," Swiss Life said in a statement.
"Accordingly, the former members have become shareholders of Swiss Life/Rentenanstalt free of charge," it added.

It said the formal transition steps were taken by the board of directors meeting on Monday, where the board approved the result of a membership ballot carried out between May 26 and June 20. Over 200,000 members or about 40 percent of a membership of around 600,000 voted.
Swiss Life said 97.1 percent or 195,158 voted yes as against 5,801 opposed, easily meeting a required quorum of two-thirds support from all valid votes.
The new board of directors is identical to the former supervisory board of the mutual insurance company.
The Swiss Life titles will be listed on the Swiss Exchange on July 3.
Swiss Life is a market leader in life insurance in Switzerland and is also established on the wider European life insurance market.
In 1996 Swiss Life's parent profit rose 21 percent to 1.37 billion francs from 1.13 billion in 1995.
The transition started in February when holders of Swiss Life participation certificates voted to convert their securities into shares.

After a transition phase with some conditional capital locked up in convertible bonds and loans, former members will wind up holding 53 percent of Swiss Life's share capital totalling 587.35 million Swiss francs or 11.7 million bearer shares with a face value of 50 SwisS francs each.

The holders of participation certificates will have eight percent and Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) 25 percent of share capital. The remaining 14 percent will be in the form of convertible bonds. -- Zurich Newsroom, +41-1-631 7340
